subject: Clarifying data residency carveouts and SLA adjustments for MeridianTech integration
messages:
From: Laura Chen <procurement@meridiantech.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@meridiantech.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MeridianTech — data residency carveouts & SLA asks

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week — MeridianTech is excited to move forward. Before we start legal, procurement asked me to surface a few specific items we need clarified in the MSA/SOW/DPA bundle:

1) Data residency carveouts — we must keep EU-origin customer data in eu-west-1; however, legacy logs that contain only metadata may be stored in the US. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports a per-customer data residency clause (we'd like to carve Europe-only subaccounts)?

2) SLA credits — procurement wants a clear on-call escalation ladder and a simpler credit formula (minutes of downtime -> % credit). The draft SLA we saw references a complicated rolling window tied to token throughput. Can legal provide an optional flat-credit table for enterprise customers?

3) Subprocessors and audit — we need an evergreen list of subprocessors and a process for notification 30 days prior to onboarding. Also want to understand whether a SOC2 report can be shared under NDA or if you have a public attestation.

4) Data flow diagram — please confirm whether request/response payloads flow through any third-party telemetry or caching services (we care about encryption-in-flight and at-rest and third-party access).

We attached a short checklist from procurement (see attachment). We can be flexible on some items, but the residency carveout + simpler SLA credits are must-haves for our procurement team.

Can we get a redline back by EOD Friday? Happy to jump on a short call.

Thanks,

Laura Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
MeridianTech
Attachment: Meridian_Procurement_Checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <procurement@meridiantech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MeridianTech — data residency carveouts & SLA asks

Hi Laura —

Appreciate the clear list. We're happy to work through these and will respond with a redline and a short proposal for the SLA credit table. Quick notes up front:

- Data residency: Redwood supports per-customer region pinning for data at rest for models and embeddings; we do keep some operational metadata in our control plane that may be replicated for reliability. We'll mark what is "customer data" vs "operational metadata" in the DPA redline.

- SLA credits: sounds reasonable to offer an optional enterprise credit schedule (flat % by downtime bucket) instead of the default rolling-window approach.

- Subprocessors & SOC2: we maintain an evergreen subprocessors list and have a SOC2 Type II report available under NDA. Vanessa (legal) will include the onboarding notification process.

I'll attach a first-pass redline of the MSA/DPA and a sketch of the data flow diagram for your architecture team to review. Can we book a 30-min call Thursday to walk through the itemized edits?

Action items for our side:
- Vanessa: legal redline with explicit clause numbers for residency carveouts and subprocessor notification.
- Infra: attach DataFlowDiagram.png showing which telemetry components touch payloads.
- Sales (Karthik): propose a mutual action plan and timeline for signature and onboarding.

Quick schedule: I can do Thu 17 Feb 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 17 Feb 15:00–16:00 PT. Which works for you?

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Head of Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Meridian_MSA_redline_v1.docx (redline)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <procurement@meridiantech.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MeridianTech — data residency carveouts & SLA asks (legal redline)

Hi Laura and team —

Attached is a legal redline of the MSA/DPA (Meridian_MSA_redline_v1.docx) and a separate SLA credit proposal (SLA_Proposal.xlsx). Below are the high-level legal positions and proposed language snippets to make review faster:

1) Data residency carveout (Section 4.2, Data Processing & Storage):
- Proposed: "Customer may elect to have Customer Data processed and stored in the region(s) listed in Exhibit A. Redwood will not move Customer Data outside elected regions except for transient operational metadata necessary for routing and availability, as described in Exhibit B."
- Note: We propose Exhibit A per-customer appendix to list regions. Exhibit B will define "operational metadata" (IP/agent health checks, anonymized metrics).

2) SLA credits (Section 7.1):
- We can offer an optional Enterprise SLA schedule (Appendix C) that maps total minutes of downtime in a calendar month to a flat credit % (e.g., 0–30min: 0%; 31–120min: 5%; 121–480min: 10%; >480min: 25%). That gives procurement the simplicity they requested.
- Exception: credits capped at monthly recurring fee.

3) Subprocessors & notification (Section 3.4):
- We agree to maintain an evergreen list and to provide 30-days prior notice for new subprocessors that will have access to Customer Data. For subprocessors that touch only anonymized telemetry we will provide a separate notification channel.

4) Audit/SOC2:
- SOC2 Type II is available under NDA. We will provide a redacted copy for procurement review and can coordinate an in-person or remote audit under standard audit scoping (charges may apply).

5) Data flow & encryption:
- Our DataFlowDiagram.png (attached) shows that request/response payloads pass through the Redwood serving runtime and a short-lived cache layer within the customer's selected region; telemetry (anonymized) is batched and sent to an internal analytics pipeline (US) for platform health. All in-flight traffic is TLS1.2+ and at-rest encryption uses AES-256.

Open/legal flags we would like confirmation on from MeridianTech:
- Whether the procurement team will accept Exhibit A as the authoritative residency list (yes/no).
- If MeridianTech requires an escrow/bring-your-own-key model for EU-only data (we can propose a KMS integration but that adds engineering time).

Please review the redline and SLA spreadsheet; I've added inline comments with clause references (e.g., [Redline: §4.2-3]). If this looks reasonable, we can move to a DocuSign workflow.

Regards,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Counsel, Partnerships & Commercial
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Meridian_MSA_redline_v1.docx (redline), SLA_Proposal.xlsx (xlsx), DataFlowDiagram.png (png)
